utterances.text: Utovic, yes. Utovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: What about Nikola Trbic was he a member?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I used to see him at the staff. But I don't know what his position was. I don't know. I did see him in the staff which does not mean that he was a member of the staff. Maybe he was in charge of security or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: What about Djordje Calosevic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Djordje Calosevic was a member of the local commune at the time. But the local commune was non-operational at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Are you saying that Djordje Calosevic was not a member of the Dalj Defence Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And you knew that for certain?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I do. Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Can we get document 1D913. This is tab number 31 on the screen. And while that's coming up, this is a publication from "Politika" dated 4 August 1991. It's titled: "More than 80 MUP and Guard Members Killed."

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: This article describes the clashes in Dalj and the take-over by the Serb forces in early August 1991, which is the same take-over we've heard from you in your statement and this morning. Now, if we look at the third paragraph of page 1 in the English, we see that it states: "According to Borivoje Milinkovic, commander ..." And there is a typo I believe, Milinovic. "According to Borivoje," as typed, "Milinovic, commander of the Dalj Defence Staff, the police and guardsmen defended themselves with all the forces they had because in their words in Dalj they were defending Zagreb." Are you aware of somebody else called Borivoje Milinovic who was a member of the Dalj Defence Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: There is Borislav Mihajlovic in Dalj who was president of the local commune, and I am Borivoje Milinovic -- Milinkovic. I don't know any Milinovic. But reporters often ascribe the wrong functions to different people. I don't know why. Maybe even to make better copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: In the original Cyrillic does it say Borivoje Milinovic or Milinkovic in this article. Could you take a look?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: It looks like Milinkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Could we, to make sure, could we blow it up a little bit? Because it's almost impossible to see what is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Do you go that it looks like Milinkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not Milinkovic. It is Milanovic. Milanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we get 65 ter document 6617 on the monitor and we'll -- we'll seek a revised translation to check this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. While we are waiting for this document, I would come back to a previous question of yours, Mr. Gillett, and the witness's answer. You asked what about Djordje Calosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Milinkovic, did you say that you are certain that this person was not a member of the Defence Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could get 65 ter document 6617, please. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Do we have a tab number, Mr. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Tab 51.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: While this is coming up, this is the record of a witness statement given in front of the county court in Osijek. Now, the witness describes his capture at the time of the Serb take-over of Dalj and then his detention and mistreatment first in Borovo Selo and then in Dalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we go to page 3 and in the B/C/S this should be at the bottom of page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: He states the following: "Their so-called Territorial Defence Staff had all the power in Dalj village and it was headed by Boro and Djordje Milinkovic, Milorad Kljajic Djordje Kljajic and Dragoljub Calosevic. They were some kind of leaders in that staff and nothing could happen in the village without their knowledge and approval, so I think they are responsible for all the crimes committed against the non-Serbian population in Dalj by the members of the Serbian paramilitary formations." Do you have a relation called Djordje Milinkovic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I have a brother or cousin.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note in the Serbian language it's not clear which.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Are you able to clarify whether he was an immediate brother to the same parents or a cousin with different parents?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: It's my brother. He was a member of the staff, and this is this information. I will repeat. Boro Milinkovic was never on the staff. This Djordje, I don't know who that name is. Mr. Calosevic, he had nothing to do with it. He was a football player and the people of Dalj know him as a athlete.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Calosevic was well known in Dalj; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Turning --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry -- sorry. Just to see two Calosevic were mentioned so far, Dragoljub, as far as I understand, and Djordje Calosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We need to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: When you say Calosevic was a football player and had nothing to do with it, what is the first name of this Calosevic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Dragoljub. Djordje is another, a different Calosevic. And those are two different persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Was Djordje Calosevic known in the Dalj village?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: We all know each other in Dalj. Djordje was also well known to all the people in Dalj. It's a very small place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Turning to the attack on Dalj on 1st of August. You say that were a pacifist; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You opposed weapons? Could you articulate your answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You said on direct testimony that you participated in the attack on Dalj by driving a truck from Borovo to Dalj; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: That truck had weapons in the back of it; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Except I didn't know immediately that it contained weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The weapons included rifles and machine-guns; right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Rifle, machine-guns. Later I saw some Thompson automatic rifles, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness be asked to speak into the microphone, not beside it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could I ask you to speak loudly and clearly for the interpreters' sake. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, you found out that the truck had weapons in the back of it when you stopped at Lovas farm, correct, which is halfway between Borovo Selo and Dalj, more or less?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Precisely that you found out at Lovas farm that the weapons were on the back of the truck?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: But you, nonetheless, went ahead and drove the weapons into Dalj.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I drove them into Dalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, could we get video 6338.2. That's the 65 ter number. And the tab is 46. And if we could play that from start to finish, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I'LL just check if the interpreters are ready for the video.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We are.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] All that is seized. We need to take care that none of the locals get hurt. We had no problems with the old timers, the native inhabitants, not even during the Second World War. We often invited them to be our guests, we socialised with them, but the others put them under pressure. We know very well who they are and what kind of people those native inhabitants are, and I think there will be no problems with them. "Reporter: Those here are the documents of a ZNG member; correct? "Answer: Yes. Look, this is evidence. Mind you that this is Marko Andabak who is Ivo Andabak's brother. You can see that this is his official ID as a reserve police member. That shows what kind of people they took into their police. He is the terrorist's brother. He participated, together with Barisic, in the murder of our ambassador Rolovic a long time ago. His brother is here as well. I mean, look what we found on him. Look. Here it says NDH, Independent State of Croatia, the letter U, and on the other side there is the text: Bitter remedy for a bitter wound. The leader. Look at this, this is interesting. The knife that was carried and the stuff they are using. "Reporter: It's a special knife and here it has a pattern for -- "Answer: Yes. This -- that's a wire for strangling or something. I must tell that you yesterday while fleeing they killed a man, a woman, and a child. I must also tell you that one of our men was trying to save small Croatian children. They were so small. He wanted to save them, but they killed him while he was trying to save them. "Reporter: We saw a few buses with Croatian refugees and children in Dalj. Does it mean they will leave these places? "Answer: Look, we have been inviting them and we are still inviting them and guarantee that they would live in peace. Today I went personally to see a mother of one Croatian MUP member. I prepared the things for them. I secured a house where they could stay. That means they can come back. It is well known who cannot come back. Ustashas that are hiding. But inhabits from here can all come and we do guarantee they would live in peace and full safety."

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You recognised the person giving the statement to the interviewer; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: For the record, could you state who it is.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: It's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The interviewer is Nimo Brajovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And in the interview, you're wearing a military jacket; right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The jacket that we just saw is a camouflage-coloured jacket; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I'll tell you all about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Well, if I can --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I had not slept all night --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I'll give you a chance to explain. I just first for the sake of the record want to clarify: Are you saying that the jacket you're wearing in this video is not a camouflage-coloured jacket? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is correct -- [indiscernible] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: -- quotation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Because on that question the witness answered, it is line 2, "I'll tell you all about it."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I'll allow the question. Please proceed --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So my first question is, are you saying that the jacket you're wearing in this clip is not a camouflage-coloured jacket?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm saying that it's not a military jacket.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Why do you say that's not a military jacket?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: It had started to rain, and I took that jacket from my brother. It's a huntsman's jacket. Yes, it is camouflage-coloured, but it was used by huntsmen when they went hunting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The first line of the video, of the audio did not come through very clearly. Could we play just the -- the first initial few seconds to get that again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] We are taking strict care that none of the captured people gets hurt. We had no problems with old time residents, not even during the second -- World War II. We often invited them to be our guests, we socialised with them, but the others put them under pressure. We know very well who they are and what kind of people these old time residents are, and I think there will be no problem with them."

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you. So you state: "We are taking strict care that none of the captured people gets hurt." Who do you mean when you say "we"?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: When I say "we," I meant us, the inhabitants of Dalj, the people who were living there. And I meant myself, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So you were responsible for the well-being of the prisoners captured during the attack on Dalj; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was not responsible. When I say "we" -- you can see that it's an informal interview that Nimo made with me in passing. I was no more responsible than any other man in the street. He could have stopped anyone in the street. I believe everybody would have told him the same as I did. I did not occupy any positions at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Some of the people captured in Dalj during the Serbia take-over were mistreated while they were in detention; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And this includes Nikola Rupcic who was beaten quite severely; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Nikola Rupcic was beaten up. One day I went to the local commune, the local commune building where the local staff was, the headquarters --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sorry to cut you off. In fact, we do have your statement and we have your evidence and this is covered in detail in your statement. So you don't need to repeat it for us again today. After the take-over of Dalj, some bodies were removed and others were left in the streets. That's correct, right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I'll repeat. After the take-over of Dalj - so this would be in August 1991 - some bodies, dead bodies, were removed but others were left lying in the streets; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: They were not removed. A refrigerator truck came from Osijek and took them to Osijek. They were supposed to collect all the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If a refrigerator truck took the bodies away, how were they not removed?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: They were driven away, removed. I understood you to mean that we took those bodies away, some there, removed them, but it was these people from Osijek who collected some of the bodies and left others behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: There were bodies at the bakery in Dalj; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I myself was not anywhere around the bakery, but I know that there were bodies around the bakery and inside the bakery. Other people told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: One of the peoples who died or whose body was at the bakery was Petar or Pero Djevelekaj. And I'll spell that: D-j-e-v-e-l-e-k-a-j. That's correct, right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: He was murdered; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: If he was murdered, then he was murdered. I don't know. I read about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You read that he was murdered? Are you saying you can confirm that he was murdered?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see it. You understand?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: That -- that wasn't my question. My question was whether you reading is that can confirm that he was murdered.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: What did you read that can confirm that he was murdered?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: There was a list of people who were murdered. He, then a neighbour of mine, and -- I don't know any more people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: What list was this?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. Which list?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You said that there was a list of people who were murdered. Which list was this?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't say a list. I read in the newspaper. I don't know for sure if it was Croatian newspapers. Sometimes somebody would bring the Glas Slavonije, the Croatian newspaper, and we would read it. And in that newspaper I read some names of people who had been murdered.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I see the time and I won't be able to go into the next point before the break, so if that's convenient. It's 12.15; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gillett. Mr. Milinkovic, we take the second break, 30 minutes as well, so we will be back at 12.45. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Welcome back, Mr. Milinkovic. Before the break, we were talking about the murder of a Mr. Petar Djevelekaj. And you knew him from Dalj, correct, prior to his murder.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: It was well-known that he was murdered; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: He -- the US Helsinki Committee in January 1992 --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And this is Exhibit P2946, which is tab 39. I'm not going to display that on the monitor, it's just for the reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: This is what they stated: "Petar Djevelekaj, a baker of Albanian origin, was first beaten and then executed by two close range gun-shots to the head." So they were correct that he was murdered; right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: When you said that Croatian newspapers such as Glas Slavonije mentioned this, when was that. What year?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say. I can't tell you the year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry. We have a technical problem with our screen in displaying e-court documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. For the moment nothing is displayed, Mr. Zivanovic, so we can -- let's check. There is something -- there is a document on the screen. Are we discussing this document, Mr. Gillett?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I didn't ask for the document to be shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So we can take this document off the screen, and then we have time to address and try to resolve your problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It is okay now. Okay. Please proceed, Mr. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Approximately what year would that have been when you read about this in the Glas Slavonije?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I really can't say. I can't even give you the year. I don't even know whether it was in Glas Slavonije. I know I read it somewhere. But I also heard people in Dalj saying that he was murdered.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So it was while you were still in Dalj. It was before you moved to Serbia; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was in Dalj all that time, up until 1996. I was there, in Dalj, all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And it was prior to you giving the statement to the OTP investigates that we've discussed today; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: While we pause, could I get 65 ter document 6620 on the monitor, please. And this is the record of examination of a witness, a different witness from the previous one I mentioned, again in front of the county court in Osijek. And this is 9 February 2001. This witness, Antun Pavosevic, was working at the bakery together with Pero Djevelekaj on the 1st of August, when the Serb take-over of Dalj occurred. In his statement, if we go to page 3, the third paragraph in English, please. And this is should be the second page in B/C/S. And, sorry, this is tab 54.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So if we look at the third paragraph, it states: "When the attack on Dalj police station stopped, I saw a group of Serbs carrying long-barrels heading towards the bakery. They started shooting at the bakery from the street before approaching. This was when Matija Zlatar and I ran out through the back door into the yard, in the vicinity of which there was a spring called Jama. The owner, Petar Djevelekaj and Nikola Tadijan, stayed inside the bakery. I hid in some rubble while Matija Zlatar hid in an abandoned pigsty. We left our hideouts at about 5.00 p.m. "From my hideout I was able to see through the same door that I ran out of what was going on at the bakery. One of the several person who came into the bakery I recognised: Marko Loncarevic, Borivoje Milinkovic, aka Vrlja, and a man named Osman, a bricklayer from Savulja in Borovo Selo. Through the same door, I saw them interrogating and mistreating Pero Djevelekaj and Nikola Tadijan. A while later I heard some shots coming from the bakery. I assumed they killed everyone inside. This later turned out to be the truth; namely, after leaving our hideouts, Matija Zlatar and I went inside the bakery and saw Pero Djevelekaj and Nikola Tadijan lying dead." Sir, your nickname is Vrlja; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And this witness was correct that Petar Djevelekaj was murdered; right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: He told the truth, that he was murdered. The rest is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You don't mention this murder or who is responsible for it your statement, do you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You were charged for this murder; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And you knew that you were charged for this murder when you gave the statement to the OTP Prosecutors; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: On 2nd of August -- actually, according to your corrections today, I believe this would be 1st August, 1991, when you arrived Dalj you went to the Dalj library; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: When I arrived Dalj I went home first. My house is at the far end of Dalj. That was around 11.00. That is, a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: After going home, you then went to the library; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned that Dalj is a town where everybody knew each other, and rumours would spread quickly in Dalj; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And you heard accounts of Arkan killing people in Dalj, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I heard but I didn't attend. I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Locals in Dalj were angered about these killings by Arkan and his men; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say that they were concerned about Arkan. They were concerned about what was going on in Dalj. The murders. I can't claim that those people were murdered by Arkan, because I didn't see it with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Are you saying the local people were not upset by Arkan's murders?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not saying that. They were upset by murders. But not Arkan's murders. By murders in general. They were concerned that there were murders in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You just mentioned that there were rumours of Arkan killing people in Dalj. So to clarify, are you saying that the locals in Dalj were not upset by the rumours of Arkan and his men killing people but they were upset about rumours of other people carrying out killings. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is asked and -- sorry. It's asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Well, with all due respect, I feel the witness has attempted to not specifically answer this question which is why I am attempting to obtain a more precise answer on this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Objection overruled. Please proceed, Mr. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Would you like me to repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no need. I'll try and be very precise. The people in Dalj were concerned by all the murders that were taking place. I personally don't know whether Arkan was doing the killings, who was it. There were murders, and people were concerned by them. If they were committed by Arkan, then they were concerned about those, and about all the other murders as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could we get Exhibit P115.1. This is tab 28 on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: This is the Vojvodina State Security Service report, describing the incident on 15 October --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gillett, it seems that tab 28 is confidential.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. This is the public version. I should have specified tab 28B, I believe, in the updated exhibit list. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, it is not report but information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Gillett? I don't see it here on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The title in English is a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The title in B/C/S is information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Say it in B/C/S, please, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: "Informacija."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Translation, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Information, report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic, interpretation says information, report. Gives the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Are you asking for -- are you asking for a --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] We'll do it. However, "report" in B/C/S is "izvjestaj."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. So you will ask for a translation verification and we will hear from you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The document states that on Thursday, 15 October, there was around 300, and I'm not quoting here, I'm paraphrasing, around 300 members of the Dalj TO forced Dalj TO Staff members and some SBWS government ministers to respond to allegations concerning the unbearable conditions. The TO members complained about Stricevic and his space police abusing and torturing prisoners, and they accused Arkan of killing 40 prisoners and he confessed to this. The report is correct when it states there were ministers of the SBWS government present at that gathering, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Did you verify with SBWS government ministers that they did not go to this gathering?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: There was nothing to verify. I am certain that none of them attended that meeting. That meeting was in Dalj, in the market-place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You don't know whether some of the SBWS government ministers went to that meeting, do you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: You're now suggesting that I don't know. I'm claiming that they were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The meeting was a large gathering with several hundred people present; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And Arkan was well-known at this time in the town of Dalj; right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The date, 15 October, is several days after two significant murder incidents in Dalj; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I learned about those murders subsequently. However, the dates and the date-wise, yes, I would say yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: It's correct that Arkan confessed to those murders at this meeting, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: It's possible. I'm not saying yes. But he was the type of a person who was capable of claiming that in front of so many people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Who told you about this gathering?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you. It was a long time ago. It was not important. I did not participate in it. I heard it from people, from neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So you don't know exactly who told you there were no government members present at this meeting, do you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Well, in fact, you're trying to minimise your knowledge of this meeting and Arkan's confession to these murders, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Just the opposite is the case. I'm against any murder, and I'm not trying to diminish Arkan's responsibility for murders, if they were committed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You're trying to diminish the responsibility of members of the SBWS government for these murders, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Not correct. Those who did it should be taken to task. Nobody from the government was there. I was the closest to the venue, because I was in Dalj, so I suppose I would have attended if anybody had.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: How do you know that you were closer to the venue than any other SBWS government member?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Because I hail from Dalj. And my office was some 500 metres away from the market-place. If anybody had come and if I -- anybody was to attend, I suppose that they would have come to fetch me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So it's a presumption that you were the closest to this meeting and that no other SBWS government member attended; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: It is a presumption. I didn't attend and I don't know that anybody else did. I'm not privy to that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, there were also stories in Dalj of Hungarians who lived on the Dalj Planina, the mountain, and that Arkan and his men had killed them as well; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct. There were two stories. I could never arrive at the bottom of any of them. There were rumours about Arkan or his men having killed them or some people who had been relocated to Dalj Planina. Although those people who lived in Dalj Planina were on good terms with us all of us Serbs in Dalj. There was no reason for anybody living there to be murdered.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Who did you hear these accounts from about Dalj killing Hungarian -- sorry, Arkan killing Hungarians in Dalj?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't give you any names. Those were rumours. People just shifted responsibility from one person to another. I heard that story on several occasions from various people, but I can't really tell you from whom. It's been a -- a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So these stories were reasonably widespread. It wasn't just yourself as an SBWS government minister that knew them; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know. I heard. It's one thing to know things and another to hear of them. I agree that other people knew as much as I did. The village was rife with that rumour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: When you say "other people," you include other members of the SBWS government, don't you.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose that others heard as well. If I heard those rumours, the others must have heard them as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And that would include Goran Hadzic; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about Goran Hadzic because people could not get to Goran that easily. Because he didn't move around market-places, stores, shops.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You're not aware of the SBWS government taking any measures to investigate or punish these murder, are you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It didn't have instruments. Even if it had wanted to, if that had been an item on the agenda, they couldn't have done anything. All of that was under the military's authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The Catholic church in Dalj was destroyed at some point, according to your statement, in 1992 or 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Do you know who destroyed the church?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I assume, because I was not present, my house is second to the Catholic church, and despite the fact that I'm a Serb and of Orthodox faith, I am emotionally attached to that church. My mother was in there. I was informed - I don't know who told me - Arkan had been seen that morning after the destruction of the church. So after the church was destroyed he was there. He was close to the place, and it is possible that he did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Did the SBWS government try and investigate who destroyed this church?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I was no longer a member of the government. I don't know when that happened. I believe that UNPROFOR had already arrived about that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So you don't know --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Could you perhaps give me the date? I believe that at the time I was no longer in the government, but could you give me the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your statement says 1992 or 1993, which is a broad range. Now, am I correct in understanding that if we are talking about the period where you were no longer a member of the government, you cannot comment on whether they were capable of investigating or not these types of crimes or not, can you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely, yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You were on the SDS board in Dalj; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And some of the other members were Borislav Mihajlovic, who you mentioned earlier today; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Branko Ocic.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Vaso Gavrilovic.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And Djordje Calosevic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And Djordje Calosevic's nickname was Djoko Briga; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Briga, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Calosevic violently abused non-Serbs in Dalj; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I heard about that. I never attended any such incident, but I did hear stories.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Is it correct or is it not correct that he violently abused non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Do you know someone called Josip Alagic from Dalj?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: It would be Alagic. Alagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Apologies for my pronunciation. Do you know this person, Josip Alagic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Was there also a second person in Dalj called Josip Alagic? It's -- as I understand -- my information, to clarify, is that one was aged 56 in 1992, and the other was aged 72 in 1992. Does that sound correct to you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I know several people by the name Alagic from Dalj. But what you're saying is quite possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could we get Exhibit P2862, this is tab 21, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And while this comes up, this is a report from UNCIVPOL from July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 6 of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: This report refers to the beating of Mr. Alagic, the 56-year-old one, in Dalj in July 1992, and it says that Djordje Calosevic beat this gentleman. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know who that person was. Is there perhaps a street or a street name? I can't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I believe the street name is it Ulica Republika which used to be known as Karadjordjevo. Does that help your memory?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So it's correct that Djordje Calosevic beat this Josip Alagic on this street, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: How do you know that's correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Because that's my uncle. A relative.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: There's no mention of Djordje Calosevic in your statement, is there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: How do you mean? When I gave my statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: In the statement that we've discussed today, there is no mention of Djordje Calosevic, is there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your statement does mention the Easter expulsion in 1992 of Croats from Dalj; right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And a gentleman named Miroslav Susic came to you on 18 April 1992 and told you they were going to drive away Croats; correct? Could you articulate your answer.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right. It was around 2.00 in the afternoon. I was at home when Mr. Susic came, a neighbour of mine, and he said they would be expelling Croats. He himself was a Croat and that's why he came to me. He wanted me to protect him. I told him he could hide at my place if he could hide anywhere, but that was impossible. Later, I heard it was true. They did expel Croats but he stayed because he was in hiding.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And it was over 100 Croats that were expelled in that incident; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number, but they were expelled. It was around Easter time, Catholic Easter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: It was a large group. It was many Croats, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I only heard on the next day that a lot of Croats had been expelled, but I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: In your statement, you described this incident in detail but you don't describe who was responsible for it. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: One of the people that was responsible was Djordje Calosevic; right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if he is responsible, but he did take part in the expulsion of Croats. I don't know who is responsible for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could I get 65 ter document 6618, this is tab 52, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And while this comes up, this is a judgement of the district court in Osijek dated 29 November 2007. One accused, a Vlastimir Dencic, is found guilty for carrying out the 18 April Easter expulsion from Dalj. The second accused, Zoran Kecman was acquitted. Now in its statement of reasons --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: That should be on page 2 in the second paragraph. And in B/C/S this should be on page 6. The English translation, I note, is only partial, but we're in the process of getting a full translation of this. We've translated the relevant portions. Page 2, the second paragraph. In the English, if we could skip to page 2. Could we skip one further page in the English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The second full paragraph reads: "In addition to that, the victims of the displacement who were examined during the trial proved in disputably that the plan about their displacement had existed and that the perpetrators were Milorad Loncarevic, Pero Djuric, Djordje Vasic, Djordje Calosevic, nicknamed Djoko Briga, Jovan Milinkovic, nicknamed Grbarvi [phoen] Jovica, Borivoje Milinkovic, nicknamed Boro Vrlja, Djordje Milinkovic, nicknamed Djordje Vrlja, and other known and unknown Arkan's Men. Emil Matin, Ivan Patron, Mirko Kelava, Andjelka Diosa, and Goran Vujicic confirmed in their statements the existence of the list of inhabitants of Dalj who were to be displaced." The judgement identified Calosevic as one of the perpetrators. That was correct, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Milorad Loncarevic was the brother of Marko Loncarevic; right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Who was Djordje Vasic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: It's a man from Dalj who worked in the local commune. Anyway, a man from Dalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So he worked for the local government.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he worked in the local commune. You could call it a local government, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Jovan Milinkovic, that's your brother; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's not my brother. It's a half-brother. I don't want to go into long explanations. He is my father's son from a first marriage.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Borivoje Milinkovic. That's yourself, correct, nicknamed Vrlja?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I was not involved in this. I did not participate in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And Djordje Milinkovic nicknamed Djordje Vrlja. That's your brother; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: He is my own brother, and he certainly did not participate in this. The two of us were not involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: There was a plan to carry out this expulsion, wasn't there, as found in the judgement?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of plan it was. You can ask the person who made that plan. I don't know of any plan. I know what I advocated all the time and what we, in the government, worked for all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, if I can stop you there. My question --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: That everyone should remain to live --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: My question was whether this expulsion was carried out according to a plan. Are you saying that there was no plan for this expulsion, that the judgement was incorrect in finding that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if there had been a plan. It probably existed, if it has proven. I don't know. I wasn't a part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this document at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 6618?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3260, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You're not aware of the SBWS authorities taking any measures to investigate or punish the perpetrators of this expulsion, are you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No. The extent of my information is that a number of policemen were involved in this expulsion as well as Arkan's Men and some civilians who also took part, which means that nothing was undertaken to stop it. Or perhaps it was impossible? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Which policemen? Were they policemen from Dalj?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Policemen from Dalj, yes. I believe that Loncarevic was employed in the local police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: On what basis do you say Arkan's Men were involved in this expulsion?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Because I heard that Arkan's Men had been there. I can tell you specifically from whom I heard that, from a Croat man who told me about it when he came to Serbia. I can even give you his name. It's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And when did he tell you about it when he came to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: He came to visit me. He had also been expelled. He came just to see me as a friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: What year would that have been?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Around year 2000, maybe 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So this was before you gave the statement to the OTP investigators?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So you knew of who was said to be responsible for this crime before you gave your statement to the OTP investigators; right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: It's not about responsibility. Responsibility lies on the person who gave the orders. Who was involved, who participated is a different thing. I only heard about some people who participated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: My question was not about who, in actual fact, was responsible. It was the fact that you knew at the time you gave your statement to the OTP investigators that people, including Arkan's Men, were said to be responsible for this crime. You knew that at the time you gave this statement, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I knew that. But nobody asked me, and ... yes, I knew that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: In your statement, paragraph 1, you state: "I will describe everything I know." You were specifically asked about this April expulsion, weren't you, and you didn't tell the investigators everything you knew about it, did you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I did not hold it back deliberately. I was tired. I spoke in bits and pieces, as I remembered things. That's why -- why I omitted it. Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You reviewed the statement before you signed it; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: It was read back to me. And that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I was not able to read it myself because it was in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: That's correct. You also read a B/C/S translation of the statement before your testimony here today; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And you didn't provide this information in your testimony earlier today, did you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I expected questions on the subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So that's a no; right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Are you saying I'm correct when I say that's a no?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't anymore what you asked me. There were two or three questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The question is quite unclear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, I -- I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The question is unclear for me. If it could be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Well -- okay. Mr. Gillett, try again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I'll try and rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The -- you did not provide information about who was responsible for this expulsion in your testimony earlier today or when you reviewed your statement yesterday, did you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I would object to this question. He was not asked today about this incident. And I don't know what is the sense of such a question. And when he was asked, he gave the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gillett, I suggest you move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Understood. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, is it fair to say that you describe the SBWS government as lacking serious powers. Would that be a fair summary of your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: In fact, the SBWS government did have a number of powers, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in certain aspects. Regarding normal life, production, the establishment of factories, culture, but certainly not control and command over the army. Nothing like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: It had a budget; correct? It had money at its disposal.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember the budget because I didn't receive a salary.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: My question was not the exact amount. It was whether the SBWS government had money at its disposal.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: A budget was passed, but there was nothing in that budget. We had only tried to collect some funds into the budget. I'm talking only about the period when I was a minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly to say earlier money was given to you as minister of culture and religion to carry out works within your ministry's remit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's not the answer that the witness gave today. He precisely said what money he got and from whom he got the money.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you better quote from the transcript, Mr. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Let me just get a minute to get that transcript reference. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. It is page 32, lines 16 to 22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And I thank my learned friend for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The answer you gave earlier today when asked whether you received a salary was: "No, I never worked for a salary. I only once got coupons for petrol that I collected in order to be able to pay the wages of the people who were working cleaning up the museum in Vukovar. That's the only thing I collected. Otherwise I worked without a salary. And I must say that money that I received I got from Mr. Milanovic. I don't know where he got it from." So there was money coming from Mr. Milanovic; correct? Could you state your answer on the record.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The SBWS government could fire members of the MUP, the police; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, the government didn't do that. I don't remember that the government fired anyone. How could the government fire anyone from the MUP? I don't even know how the Ministry of Interior, how the police, were financed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Are you saying you don't remember that the government fired anyone from the MUP or that they could not fire anyone from the MUP?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was at lower levels. There were secretariats at the lower level.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: That wasn't my question. My question was whether you're saying you don't remember if the SBWS government fired anyone from the MUP or whether it was not possible, they didn't have the power to fire anyone, from the MUP?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think it is also unclear. The MUP is too -- too vague. What does it mean? For ordinary policemen or some -- someone with some function or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I can try and clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I understand your answer to you be I don't remember that they could fire people from the MUP. Would that include any incidents of any police within the SBWS, that you don't remember any instances of the SBWS government being able to fire any of those police?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Some ministers were replaced. You must understand that the government makes proposals to the assembly and the assembly accepts them or not. We did not deal with personnel affairs in the police force in depth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: When you say "we did not deal with personnel affairs in the police force," you're meaning the ministers of the SBWS government and the prime minister; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Ministers and the prime minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could I get document P251.245.1. And this should be the public version of tab 33.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is the decision on the dismissal of the secretary of the SUP dated 16 October 1991. And it states: "During its session on 16 October 1991, and in accordance with Article 2, paragraph 1, item 6 on the Law on The government of the Serb Region of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srijem, the government of the Serb region of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srijem has passed a decision on the dismissal of the secretary of the Vukovar Secretariat of Interior." This is signed by the prime minister, Goran Hadzic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But this was the beginning, the early days, the 16th of October. That position of secretary was still very high at that time. So this can very well be true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So when you gave your answer that "we did not deal with personnel affairs in the police force in depth," you were talking about a period after 16 October 1991; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: When I say "in depth," I mean at the lower levels. This must have been done at the proposal of the minister, the government must have approved it, and then the prime minister signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You haven't answered my question. My question was about whether, during the period up to 16 October 1991, the SBWS government was able to deal with personnel affairs in the police force; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In my understanding, the witness already answered this question. He did not limit his answer on any -- any time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness's answer agreed with me, that it was signed by Goran Hadzic. This is at line 22. But then he said: "But this was the beginning, the early days, the 16th of October." I want to verify whether he's making a distinction in the period of time as to when the government did or not -- did or did not have powers in relation to the police in SBWS.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: However, again, the police force is too wide. It is not -- it is vague. And he said we didn't went to depth. So -- so -- so I -- I -- I think it should be more precise. This question should be more precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I'll allow the question, Mr. Zivanovic. And, afterwards, after the answer, we can perhaps go into the issue of high-ranking police officers or -- and -- and low-ranking ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: If we don't, we get composed questions and problems with the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Firstly, it's correct that up to 16 October 1991 the SBWS government, including Goran Hadzic, did deal with personnel matters of the SBWS police; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry. Again, it is a personal matters. As far as I see these are not personal matters. It is appointments, official appointment, or a dismissal. I don't believe that it is personal matters. That we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I think I heard personnel, not personal matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, okay. Sorry. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Correct. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So I'm talking about matters of employment hiring and firing. And it's correct that the SBWS government and Mr. Hadzic could deal and did deal with those matters up until 16 October 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So you're saying that they did not take this decision on the dismissal of the secretary of the Vukovar SUP on 16 October 1991?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not saying that. I didn't say that. However, I may not even have been at the session of the government when that was decided. I never attended a session that would discuss personnel issues at the police. There was just one secretary of the SUP. There were not several SUP secretaries. It was at the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Again, sir, that's not the question I asked. The question I'm asking is: Based on this document in front of us, we can see that on 16 October 1991 the SBWS government and the prime minister did take a measure related to the hiring and firing of the secretary of the Vukovar SUP; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: It is correct according to this document. But I don't remember this discussion, discussion on Milakovic's appointment or dismissal. I don't remember. Maybe I was simply not there. We never discussed any such matters, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: In terms of police of lower ranks, did the SBWS government have powers to hire or fire those police?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. That was within the purview of secretaries, lower-ranking commanders, and so on and so forth. They had a say in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If the SBWS government could hire or fire higher-ranking police members, such as this secretary, then they could influence the hiring or firing of local police as well, couldn't they?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No. There was too much other work to leave room for things like this. No, they never dealt with those issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: My question wasn't whether they dealt with those issues in actual fact. It's whether they had the power to influence decisions concerning lower-level police. And that's not the question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could have a clarification what does it mean "had the power to influence"? I really don't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honours, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I must admit that I'm at a loss as well, Mr. Gillett. I mean, is that a power, what are you talking about now; namely, that by -- by -- by hiring or firing a higher-ranking officer they can indirectly, et cetera, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I mean, is that relevant for the witness to -- for -- is it that relevant? Is it appropriate for this witness to answer these kind of questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I -- I think we've exhausted this line of inquiry on this issue. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Turning to the TO which you do mention in your statement and you've mentioned a number of times today. You don't know whether the SBWS minister of defence had power over the TO, do you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So you can't comment on the SBWS government's ability to command or control the TO, can you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: The government did not control the TO. The TO was a reserve force of the JNA, which means that the JNA, i.e., the military, commanded the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: That statement requires you to know that the SBWS minister of defence could not control the TO; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, he could not. He was not in a position to do that. I repeat -- let's make things clear. There's a period when I was minister, and there is a period after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, can we look at paragraph 63 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And again, this is 1D2328. It's tab 1 for the Prosecution exhibits. 63.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You say: "The TO was not under the control of the SAO SBWS government. The TO was under the control of the JNA officers in the field. It is possible that the minister of defence might have had some authority over the TO. However, I don't really know about this." Did I read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE MILINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see the time. I could start a new line, but because it involves different documents, I wonder if we should take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And how long would you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Remaining in cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If I could get an estimate from the Registrar kindly as to how much I've used, that may help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: 30 minutes left, Mr. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And is that 30 minutes left out of four hours? Am I understanding right, I've used three and a half hours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I suppose that's how the calculation is made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You're right to ask that, Mr. Gillett. You have one hour and 30 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you. I would predict that I could finish within an hour. I have one -- at least one major subject to go into still with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Milinkovic, we finish here for the day and for the week. So we expect you to be back on Monday at 9.00. In the meantime, you remain under oath, and that means two things: First of all, you cannot have any contact with any of the parties; and second, you cannot discuss your testimony with anybody, in the street, or in the hotel, or whatever. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 15th day of September, 2014, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
